note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Hierarchical concept model leads to task-vector retrieval theory: QA training retrieves task vectors, ICL-only training memorizes low-level features

nodes.name: Task vector enables vector arithmetic in ICL
nodes.description: LLMs form a task vector in intermediate layers during in-context learning, and factual-recall ICL follows a residual vector arithmetic f(x_query) = a_f + b_query, analogous to Word2Vec arithmetic.

nodes.name: Latent geometry is approximately additive
nodes.description: In GPT2-medium embeddings, answer vectors align more strongly with the task vector than query vectors do, so x + task vector approximately equals y (Fig 1).

nodes.name: Hierarchical concept data model
nodes.description: The theory models word embeddings with high-level task concepts, low-level concepts and irrelevant concepts, where the task vector is the high-level concept component.

nodes.name: Gap in existing ICL theory
nodes.description: Existing ICL theories overlook the residual stream or treat it unnaturally, rely on linearized attention or squared/hinge losses, and lack a theoretical account of why QA training data enables factual recall.

nodes.name: GD on residual transformer retrieves task vectors
nodes.description: Nonlinear transformers with softmax attention, MLP, layer normalization and residual connections trained by gradient descent on cross-entropy loss can perform factual-recall ICL via vector arithmetic despite non-convexity (Thm 3.2).

nodes.name: ICL-trained models memorize low-level features
nodes.description: When training and testing on word-label ICL data, the transformer fails to reliably retrieve the high-level task vector; the output becomes a hybrid vector contaminated by low-level features (harmful memorization), as in Fig 2(d).

nodes.name: QA training retrieves the task vector
nodes.description: Models trained on QA data learn the task vector, achieving arbitrarily small test error on both word-label ICL and QA-ICL prompts, because low-level features b_k are absent from QA data (Thm 3.2, Prop 3.3, Fig 3).

nodes.name: Task vector regression from demonstrations
nodes.description: The trained transformer can approximately retrieve the task vector solely from demonstration pairs without requiring a query word.

nodes.name: Task vector arithmetic adds to any query
nodes.description: The retrieved intermediate vector can be added to any query sharing the co-task concept to give the correct answer with test loss at most epsilon.

nodes.name: Compositional OOD generalization
nodes.description: A QA-trained model generalizes to unseen dictionaries (new conic combinations of task vectors with new orthogonal features) and to prompts with multiple co-task concepts (fewer than 4) and varied length (Prop 3.4).

nodes.name: Multi-concept prompts give weighted task vectors
nodes.description: With multiple co-task concepts in a prompt, the model forms a softmax-weighted convex combination of task vectors, resembling Bayesian model averaging.

nodes.name: Simulations corroborate theory
nodes.description: Simulations with K=2, K'=100, d=3000 show the QA-trained model avoids the persistent constant test error (0.2) of the ICL-trained model (Fig 2-3).

isolated_nodes.name: Limited to single-token settings
isolated_nodes.description: The framework is limited to single-token settings and idealized assumptions, and does not study how task vectors emerge in deeper layers.

structural_reasoning: Argument builds from empirical vector-arithmetic geometry to a hierarchical concept model and optimization theory showing QA-trained transformers retrieve task vectors and generalize OOD.
